                    ### Question
                    In the processing and presentation of peptides of extracellular origin intervene (n):

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the processing and presentation of extracellular peptides, several key components are involved. TAP proteins (Transporter associated with Antigen Processing) transport peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) where they are loaded onto MHC class I molecules for presentation to CD8+ T cells. Tapasina assists in the loading of peptides onto MHC class I, ensuring effective presentation. HLA-DM is crucial for loading peptides onto MHC class II molecules, facilitating their presentation to CD4+ T cells. The proteasome degrades extracellular proteins into peptides, which are then presented on MHC class I molecules. HLA-B molecules are a type of MHC class I molecule that presents these peptides to T cells. Therefore, the correct options are TAP proteins, tapasina, HLA-DM, and HLA-B molecules, while the proteasome is involved in peptide generation rather than direct presentation.
